question:
During a classroom activity, two teams record six numerical observations in the same arrangement. Their records are represented by $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&4\\3&5&0\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-3\\4&-1&6\end{bmatrix}$. Each matrix has two rows and three columns. The teacher asks the students to interchange rows and columns to form transposes and also to combine the two records by adding corresponding entries. The purpose of the activity is to compare the result obtained by first adding the matrices and then taking the transpose with the result obtained by transposing the matrices separately and then adding them.

(a) Find the transpose $A^T$ of matrix $A$.

(b) Calculate $A+B$.

(c) Determine $(A+B)^T$.

(d) Calculate $A^T+B^T$ and verify whether it is equal to $(A+B)^T$.
explanation:
(a)
The transpose of a matrix is obtained by interchanging its rows and columns. Therefore, for $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&4\\3&5&0\end{bmatrix}$, we get $A^T=\begin{bmatrix}2&3\\-1&5\\4&0\end{bmatrix}$.

(b)
Since $A$ and $B$ have the same order, their addition is defined. Adding corresponding elements, $A+B=\begin{bmatrix}2+1&-1+2&4-3\\3+4&5-1&0+6\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3&1&1\\7&4&6\end{bmatrix}$.

(c)
Interchanging the rows and columns of $A+B=\begin{bmatrix}3&1&1\\7&4&6\end{bmatrix}$ gives $(A+B)^T=\begin{bmatrix}3&7\\1&4\\1&6\end{bmatrix}$.

(d)
First, $B^T=\begin{bmatrix}1&4\\2&-1\\-3&6\end{bmatrix}$. Therefore, $A^T+B^T=\begin{bmatrix}2+1&3+4\\-1+2&5-1\\4-3&0+6\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3&7\\1&4\\1&6\end{bmatrix}$. This is exactly the matrix obtained in part (c). Hence, $(A+B)^T=A^T+B^T$ for the given matrices.
